hypothesis: Setting EVOVS_SCREEN_JOBS to 8 will reduce screening.rank latency enough to meet min_speedup while preserving equivalent rankings.
risk: Increased job parallelism may cause resource contention or nondeterministic ranking behavior that violates equivalence or max_time_ratio acceptance.

verdict.decision: REJECTED — the implementation regressed on measurement; reverted, no knob shipped
verdict.method: operator-side measurement following the shadow protocol, baseline replayed on current code (the recorded trace numbers are stale)

measurements.note: featurize uses its own 8-way process pool
2.4x slower: the outer pool forces EVOVS_FEAT_JOBS=1 inside each worker
second run 30.0s under machine load; both far below the 73.7s corpus median

verdict.root_cause: rdkit.featurize is already chunk-parallel (EVOVS_FEAT_JOBS=8, candidate1 promoted 2026-11-06) and dominates the step. Chunking the outer loop serializes exactly the stage that was already parallel, and adds one 822 MB feature matrix per worker.
verdict.corpus_confound: The 73.7s median predates that promotion: the corpus mixes pre- and post-promotion runs, so the latency evidence was stale before the candidate was even drafted.
verdict.what_the_measurement_says_now: screening.rank on 100k currently runs ~18-30s: featurize ~9s (parallel), predict_proba ~7s (xgboost, already multithreaded), rest is I/O. There is no 1.3x win behind an outer-pool knob.
follow_ups: evolution/propose.py records corpus_window and a caveat, and requires calls from at least two tickets
evolution/shadow.py gained --baseline-replay so a latency claim is measured on current code, not on a recorded number
verdict.implementation: reverted (git checkout scientific/src/evovs_science/screening/predict.py); nothing shipped, no behaviour change
